shouldFix.title: The gate scan that landed CLAUDE-PONGJ-V2-SF2 at v3 has been deleted, so seven whole-gate-set assertions are again supported against three gates — and the disposition table still reports that finding as accepted at the field that no longer holds it
shouldFix.finding: Every class asserts existingGate 'none'. That is a claim about the entire live condition-4 gate set, not about three gates, and it is the claim the artifact exists to establish. At v3 it was supported: closestGateScan named five gates with reasons, four of the five claims byte-exact, and a catch-all enumerating DR-G01..G08, G11, G13..G19, G22, which I expanded programmatically and confirmed covered all 22 live ids with nothing missing and nothing invented. That is what closed my CLAUDE-PONGJ-V2-SF2 and it is a large part of why I accepted v3. In v4 closestGateScan is no longer an array at all; it is the string 'Superseded by g20Quoted / g21Quoted / classes.*.g20g21Join. The v3 short characterizations of G20/G21 are withdrawn.' Measured: only DR-G10, DR-G20 and DR-G21 appear anywhere in v4's bytes; nineteen gates are unmentioned, among them DR-G09 and DR-G12, which v3 had quoted byte-exactly. The withdrawal is also wider than its own stated scope — the note says the G20/G21 short characterizations are withdrawn, but what was actually removed includes the G09 and G12 entries and the 17-id catch-all, which had nothing to do with the Codex finding. Alongside that, authorityClaim dropped the clause 'no live DR-G* cell owns those classes as written', so the artifact's central conclusion now survives only as seven per-class flags with no stated basis beyond three gates. Compounding it, findingDisposition still records CLAUDE-PONGJ-V2-SF2 as ACCEPTED with landedAt 'closestGateScan' — a field that now explicitly supersedes its own content. A coordinator reading that table would record a finding as answered when its answer has been withdrawn.
shouldFix.whyNotBlocker: Nothing asserted is false. I have now read all 22 live gate claims four times across this family and the universal negative holds: no live gate owns host-side relation-registry admission, policy or threshold refusal, Coverage-domain sufficiency, or RequestId/ExecutionId allocation. The defect is that the artifact no longer shows this, and misreports that it does.
shouldFix.whyNotADemandForSomethingNew: This is not a fresh requirement. It is the restoration of a repair that was already made, reviewed and accepted at v3, removed in the course of answering a different reviewer's different point. The two repairs are complementary: depth on G20/G21 and breadth across the gate set answer different questions, and nothing about quoting two rows in full requires deleting the enumeration of the other nineteen.
shouldFix.repair: Keep everything v4 added and restore what v3 had. Return closestGateScan to an array: the G09 and G12 entries with their byte-exact claims, the catch-all enumerating DR-G01..G08, G11, G13..G19, G22 with its shared reason, and — if the G10/G20/G21 short characterizations are genuinely superseded — a pointer from those three entries to g10Quoted, g20Quoted and g21Quoted rather than deletion. Restore 'no live DR-G* cell owns those classes as written' to authorityClaim. Then correct findingDisposition so CLAUDE-PONGJ-V2-SF2's landedAt names the restored field.

advisories.title: NT-6's rationale says D-078 'owns invented D9 codes', which inverts on a careless read
advisories.finding: NT-6's whyNotOwner ends 'D-078 still owns invented D9 codes.' D-078 is the owner-record of the DR-007 preview Route B disposition; its own text gives the owner role as 'D9 authority + evidence/retention owner' and states 'Invents no D9 code.' The intended point is right and well sourced — D9 authority sits at DR-007/D-078, not at DR-G21 and not at DR-133, which is also what the v3 contract's own NT-6 pass condition says with 'Mapping remains DR-007 / v1.14 host-owned'. But as written the sentence can be read as D-078 authorising invented D9 codes, the opposite of what D-078 says.

advisories.repair: Rephrase to track D-078's words: 'D9 authority remains owned at DR-007 / D-078; this artifact invents no D9 code.'

independence.priorPosition: I accepted v3. Rejecting v4 after accepting its predecessor needs care in both directions: I must not defend my acceptance by waving through a successor, and I must not invent an objection to look consistent. The finding here is neither — it is that a repair I verified at v3 has been removed, which I established by diffing v4 against v3 field by field and by searching v4's bytes for all 22 gate ids, and which the artifact's own disposition table still reports as present.
independence.notEscalated: I did not treat the deletion as a blocker, because the conclusion it supported is true on my own measurement, and I did not object to any part of the new G20/G21 material, which is the best work in the family so far.

coordinatorSummary: REJECT at 0 blockers, 1 SHOULD-FIX and 1 advisory. Twelve attacks run, three landed, none a blocker. Custody is clean: subject 17da1678 at 0444 unmoved, v1 through v3 all still frozen with their own prompt paths, HEAD never left 2d1254e, and every cited digest reproduces. The new work is the best this artifact has had. G20 and G21 are now quoted at all eight cells each plus their D-086 executes text, and 24 of 24 gate-cell strings across G10, G20 and G21 are byte-exact against the live rows, as are both d086Executes strings against gate-harness-naming.v3. The ownership-versus-execution-adjacent-overlap frame is the right one and is applied honestly: every existingGateOwnsTheDR133Law is false, and each overlap claim traces to a quoted string — 'malformed/truncated' in G21's corpus, 'candidate discard' and 'Coverage/D9/UI/exit goldens' in its retained evidence, 'final authority' and 'authority escape' for G20. The whyNotOwner lines hold the correct line between what containment must produce after a component fails and refusal of authority asserted on a well-formed path. What blocks is that this depth was paid for with breadth. At v3, closestGateScan enumerated five gates with reasons plus a catch-all covering DR-G01..G08, G11, G13..G19, G22, which I expanded programmatically and confirmed covered all 22 live ids; that block is what closed my CLAUDE-PONGJ-V2-SF2 and much of why I accepted v3. In v4 it is a superseded-note string, and only DR-G10, DR-G20 and DR-G21 appear anywhere in the file — nineteen gates are unmentioned, including DR-G09 and DR-G12, which v3 quoted byte-exactly and which had nothing to do with the Codex finding, so the withdrawal is wider than its own stated scope. authorityClaim also dropped 'no live DR-G* cell owns those classes as written', leaving the artifact's central conclusion as seven per-class flags with a basis shown for three gates. And findingDisposition still records CLAUDE-PONGJ-V2-SF2 as ACCEPTED at closestGateScan, a field that now supersedes its own content, so the table would tell a coordinator a finding is answered when its answer has been withdrawn. I read all 22 live claims a fourth time and the universal negative still holds, which is why this is a SHOULD-FIX rather than a blocker: the artifact is not wrong, it has stopped showing its work and misreports that it hasn't. The two repairs are complementary — nothing about quoting two rows in full requires deleting the enumeration of the other nineteen — so a v5 that keeps every one of v4's additions and restores the scan, the authorityClaim clause and the correct landedAt would, on what I can measure, accept. The advisory is that NT-6's 'D-078 still owns invented D9 codes' inverts on a careless read, since D-078 records D9 authority and states it invents no D9 code.
